title: A separated presheaf injects into its plus construction
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal G$ be a separated presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$: for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$, the map $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)$, $s\mapsto(s|_{U_i})_i$, is injective. Let $\mathcal G^+$ be the plus construction and $\theta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^+$ the canonical map [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]. Then $\theta_{\mathcal G,U}:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal G^+(U)$ is injective for every object $U$.

source.place: Sites, Definition 00WA (definition-separated) and Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), part (2), proof of item-sheaf

proof.text: *Equal images under $\theta$ agree on a covering.* Let $a,b\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $\theta_{\mathcal G,U}(a)=\theta_{\mathcal G,U}(b)$ in $\mathcal G^+(U)$. The case of $\theta$ in clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf], applied to the presheaf $\mathcal G$, gives a covering $\{v_k:V_k\to U\}_{k\in K}$ of $U$ with $a|_{V_k}=b|_{V_k}$, i.e. $\mathcal G(v_k)(a)=\mathcal G(v_k)(b)$, for all $k\in K$. (This is where the colimit defining $\mathcal G^+(U)$ is used: it is filtered, so two elements of $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(U)$ with the same class already agree after pulling back to some covering $\mathcal V$ along the unique morphism of coverings $\mathcal V\to\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$.)

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), proof of part (2) (item-sheaf), first sentence; Definition 00WA (definition-separated)

proof.text: *Separatedness.* By Step 1 the elements $a$ and $b$ have the same image $(a|_{V_k})_k=(b|_{V_k})_k$ under the map $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_{k\in K}\mathcal G(V_k)$, $s\mapsto(s|_{V_k})_k$, of the covering $\{V_k\to U\}_{k\in K}$. Since $\mathcal G$ is separated, this map is injective (the hypothesis of the statement, for this covering), so $a=b$. As $a,b$ were arbitrary, $\theta_{\mathcal G,U}$ is injective, for every object $U$. (Stacks phrases this as: every canonical map $\mathcal G(U)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$ is injective for a separated $\mathcal G$, the map $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\subset\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)$ being an inclusion.)
